solicitations.title: Grounds Maintenance Dale Bumpers National Rice Research Center Stuttgart, AR
solicitations.description: Reference Solicitation No. 127EAV26Q0121 (1172840) Project Title: Grounds Maintenance Dale Bumpers National Rice Research Center Stuttgart, AR Unit: ARS This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial items prepared in accordance with the format in FAR Part 12. Solicitation number 127EAV26Q0121 is issued as a Request for Quotation (RFQ) for Grounds Maintenance at The Dale Bumpers National Rice Research Center Stuttgart, AR. This acquisition is 100% set-aside for small business concerns. The applicable North American Industry Classification Standard Code is 561730 Landscaping Services. The small business size standard is $9.5M. All responsible sources may submit a quotation which will be considered by the agency. The Government intends to award one firm fixed price contract with a base year and 4 one-year option periods. The Contractor shall provide all Materials, Supplies, Supervision, transportation and incidentals necessary to perform mowing services at The Dale Bumpers National Rice Research Center per attached Statement of Work (SOW). The scope of the work required under this contract consists of mowing/trimming of grounds to assure a good, well-maintained appearance on an ongoing basis. Award of the option years are contingent upon the availability of funds. The Government reserves the right not to exercise the option years listed in this solicitation or resulting contract. The Contractor shall not be entitled to any compensation, claim, or equitable adjustment for unawarded option years including anticipated profit or lost opportunity. Location: 2890 Hwy 130 East Stuttgart, AR 72160 ***PRE- AWARD QUESTIONS- Any questions regarding the Request for Quotation (RFQ) shall be emailed to the Contract Specialist Shavera Leveille no later than 1700 CST 9/9/2026. THERE WILL BE NO QUESTIONS ALLOWED AFTER THIS TIME. All quotes shall be emailed to shavera.leveille@usda.gov no later than 1700 CST 9/15/2026, or sooner. Site visits are encouraged, but not mandatory to confirm locations, dimensions, and conditions of the project before a bid is submitted. A Site Visit will be held on 9/8/2026 at 10:00 A.M. CST at 2890 Hwy 130 East Stuttgart, AR 72160. The site visit shall be for the purpose of observing firsthand any conditions relevant to the completion of this project. No consideration will be given to claims based on lack of knowledge of existing conditions. Set-Aside: 100% Total Small Business Evaluation and Basis for Award: See attached Instructions to Offerors POC for this solicitation is Shavera Leveille at shavera.leveille@usda.gov.

solicitations.description: ----------------Amendment A0003-------------- The purpose of Amendment A0003 is to: 1) Incorporate the following revised attachments based upon questions received. -Attachment 01 A0001 Turn Key Facility PWS (NON-IHSC) -Attachment 01a A0001 Facility Specific Requirements -Attachment 01b A0001 Facility Specific Requirements -Attachment 02 A0001 Turn Key Facility PWS (IHSC) -Attachment 04 A0001 Solicitation Question and Answer Government Response -Attachment 10b A0001 Anticipated Transportation Routes Requirement B -Attachment 15 A0001 Turn Key Pricing Spreadsheet All other terms and conditions remainunchanged. ----------------Amendment A0002-------------- The government is in receipt of questions from industry and is the process of drafting responses to questions received and revising applicable attachments. A future amendment (A0003) will be issued to incorporate government responses and amended attachments tomorrow, 9/11/26. The purpose of Amendment A0002 is to: 1) Extend proposal submission due date and time to 9/14/26 at 5:00 PM ET. All other terms and conditions remain unchanged. ----------------Amendment A0001-------------- The purpose of Amendment A0001 is to: 1) Revise sections of the PWS. See Attachment 01 A0001 - Turnkey Facility PWS (Non-IHSC) (Requirements A- Denver, B -Miami and C-Philadelphia), and Attachment 02 A0001 - Turnkey Facility PWS (IHSC) (Requirement D-Seattle). 2) Add the following attachments: Attachment 15 Turn-key pricing Spreadsheet. All other terms and conditions remain unchanged. ----------------------------------------------------------------------- Combined Synopsis/Solicitation The Department of Homeland Security, U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement, Office of Acquisition Management, Detention Compliance and Removals, is issuing Request for Proposal (RFP) No. 70CDCR26R00000026 for multiple turnkey detention facility requirements. ICE intends to award separate single-award Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contracts for the provision of comprehensive detention facility services, transportation services, food services, operations and maintenance services, and related support services for ICE detainees in Enforcement and Removal Operations custody. The Government may make one or more awards under this solicitation. Each requirement/facility will be evaluated and awarded separately. The anticipated contract type for each requirement is a hybrid Firm-Fixed-Price and Labor-Hour IDIQ contract. Each contract is anticipated to include a 120-month ordering period, inclusive of a 60-day transition period. The Government is also evaluating the option to extend services for up to six months pursuant to FAR 52.217-8. The solicitation includes the following requirements/facilities: Requirement A: Denver Area of Responsibility Requirement B: Miami Area of Responsibility Requirement C: Philadelphia Area of Responsibility Requirement D: Seattle Area of Responsibility Requirements A, B, and C are for Non-IHSC-staffed facilities. Requirement D is for an IHSC-staffed facility. Description of Requirement The Contractor shall furnish the proposed detention facility and provide all management, supervision, personnel, labor, equipment, vehicles, supplies, materials, and services necessary to provide safe, secure, humane, and compliant detention services for ICE detainees. Services shall be provided 24 hours per day, 7 days per week, 365 days per year. The required services include, but are not limited to: Turnkey detention facility operations; Secure custody, care, supervision, and safekeeping of detainees; Facility management and administration; Staffing, supervision, training, and quality control; Food service operations; Armed transportation services; On-call guard services; Intake, release, classification, detainee accountability, and detainee property management; Facility security and control operations; Video surveillance and related security systems; Virtual attorney visitation capability and operation; Legal access, law library access, and group legal orientation space; Religious services, recreation, disability accommodations, and language access; Commissary operations; Emergency response, evacuation planning, and continuity of operations; Operations and maintenance, including preventive and corrective maintenance; Fire, life safety, environmental, sanitation, pest control, utility, accessibility, and physical plant compliance; Records management, reporting, data ownership, and information security compliance; Compliance with applicable ICE detention standards, ACA ALDF standards, PREA requirements, and other applicable federal requirements. For Non-IHSC-staffed facilities, the Contractor shall also provide comprehensive health care services in accordance with the applicable Performance Work Statement, facility-specific requirements, ICE detention standards, and related requirements. For the IHSC-staffed facility, ICE Health Services Corps will provide health services, and the Contractor shall provide required facility support, space, security, and related services. The Contractor shall also provide and maintain required ICE, IHSC, OPLA, USCIS, EOIR, and other administrative and support spaces as applicable to the specific requirement and facility-specific addenda. Applicable Standards and Compliance Requirements Performance shall comply with the requirements set forth in the solicitation, Performance Work Statements, facility-specific requirements, and all applicable attachments. These include, but are not limited to: Applicable ICE detention standards; American Correctional Association Adult Local Detention Facility standards; DHS Prison Rape Elimination Act standards; Architectural Barriers Act and Rehabilitation Act requirements; Occupational Safety and Health Administration requirements; Fire, life safety, building, and environmental requirements; DHS and ICE information security, privacy, records, and data protection requirements; Applicable transportation, firearms, body armor, licensing, and credentialing requirements; Applicable federal, state, and local laws and regulations, except where federal requirements control. The Contractor shall obtain and maintain required permits, licenses, approvals, certifications, inspections, and accreditations necessary for performance. Phase 1 and Phase 2 Evaluation Process The Government intends to conduct this procurement using a multi-phase proposal submission and evaluation process. Phase 1 Phase 1 consists of: Volume I, Administration Volume II, Readiness Screening Phase 1 will be evaluated on a pass/fail basis for each proposed facility. Offerors must receive a Pass for every Phase 1 criterion for a facility in order to advance to Phase 2 for that facility. Phase 1 readiness criteria include: Legal control of the proposed facility; Minimum beds and required configuration; Building, fire, life safety, and occupancy; Zoning, licensing, and local approvals; Staffing pipeline and training readiness; Key leadership and core security/control systems; Transportation assets and equipment; Environmental and site information, including information required to support the Government’s NEPA review. A Phase 1 Pass notice does not constitute award, approval of the proposed facility, an affirmative responsibility determination, or completion of the Government’s NEPA review. Phase 2 Phase 2 consists of: Volume III, Technical Proposal Technical and Management Approach Corporate Experience Volume IV, Price Proposal Only offerors and facilities that receive a Phase 1 Pass will be invited to submit Phase 2 proposals for the applicable facility. Basis for Award For each requirement/facility, the Government intends to award a single-award IDIQ contract to the responsible offeror whose conforming proposal provides the best value to the Government, considering price and non-price factors. This acquisition will use a tradeoff approach and is not a Lowest Price Technically Acceptable acquisition. The Government may select a proposal other than the lowest-priced proposal when the evaluated benefits merit the additional price. The Government may award based on initial proposals without discussions. Offerors are encouraged to submit their best technical and price terms in their initial proposal. Proposal Submission Offerors may propose for one, more than one, or all four requirements/facilities. Offerors submitting proposals for multiple facilities shall provide separately identifiable proposal content for each facility. Information submitted for one facility will not be assumed to apply to another facility unless expressly cross-referenced and demonstrated to be applicable. Each volume shall be complete and self-contained so the Government can evaluate the applicable phase, volume, or factor independently. Questions and Proposal Due Dates Questions and proposals shall be submitted in accordance with Section L of the solicitation. The anticipated submission dates are: Solicitation Questions: September 4, 2026, at 2:00 p.m. Eastern Time Phase 1 Proposal, Volume I and Volume II: September 11, 2026, at 5:00 p.m. Eastern Time Phase 2 Proposal, Volume III and Volume IV: Estimated September 18, 2026, at 5:00 p.m. Eastern Time, or as otherwise established in Phase 2 invitations The Government may revise these dates through amendment or written notice. Questions shall be submitted using Attachment 04, Solicitation Question Template . Questions and proposals shall be submitted by email to both of the following addresses: Shane Crowl: Shane.Crowl@ice.dhs.gov oaqdcr@ice.dhs.gov The email subject line shall reference Solicitation No. 70CDCR26R00000026 . Attachments The solicitation includes multiple attachments, including Performance Work Statements, facility-specific requirements, QASP/PRS documents, pricing templates, transportation requirements, privacy and records requirements, PREA requirements, physical plant requirements, medical services requirements, labor standards, DSCS materials, and NEPA procedural guidance. Offerors are responsible for reviewing the solicitation and all attachments in their entirety. Additional Information This solicitation does not commit the Government to pay any costs incurred in the preparation or submission of proposals, questions, studies, designs, or other proposal-related materials. All public disclosures regarding this procurement shall be handled in accordance with applicable solicitation requirements and DHS/ICE public affairs procedures.

solicitations.title: FUEL FILTER
solicitations.description: The United States Coast Guard Surface Forces Logistics Center has a requirement and requesting quotations for the following 1.NSN:2910 01 731 9862 QTY: 240 ea FUEL FILTER MFG NAME: ROLLS ROYCE SOLUTIONS GMBH PART_NUMBER # X59408300151 EACH ITEM SHALL BE INDIVIDUALLY PRESERVED AND PACKAGED AS APPROPRIATE IN ACCORDANCE WITH MIL-STD-2073-1E METHOD 10. MARKING IAW MIL-STD-129R EXCEPT BAR CODED IAW ISO/IEC-16388-2007, CODE 39 SYMBOLOGY. ALL MARKINGS SHALL BE PLACED SO VISIBLE BY FORKLIFT OPERATOR, IF APPLICABLE. ALL ITEMS ARE INSPECTED WHEN DELIVERED TO THE COAST GUARD WAREHOUSE. FAILURE TO MEET THE REQUIREMENTS FOR PACKAGING, PACKING, MARKING (PP&M) AND BAR-CODING WILL RESULT IN THE ITEM(S) BEING REJECTED AND POSSIBLY RETURNED TO THE VENDOR. THIS WILL DELAY PAYMENT. ANY QUESTIONS CONCERNING THE PP&M REQUIREMENTS OR BAR-CODING SHOULD BE ADDRESSED WITH THE CONTRACTING OFFICER PRIOR TO CONTRACT AWARD. Delivery shall be F.O.B. DESTINATION to USCG Surface Forces Logistics Center, 2401 Hawkins Point Road, Baltimore MD 21226 Required delivery date no later than: 9/30/26 This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for a commercial item prepared in accordance with the format outlined in FAR Subpart 12.6, FAC 2025-06 and as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation. Quotations are being requested and a written solicitation will not be issued. The NAICS code for this solicitation is 333618 and the business size standard is 750. The resultant purchase order will be awarded using simplified acquisition procedures in accordance with FAR 13 All responsible sources may submit a quotation via email to Nina.m.crosby@uscg.mil, which if timely received, shall be considered by the Agency. Companies must have valid DUNS numbers and be registered with SYSTEMS FOR AWARD MANAGEMENT (SAM) and shall provide the company Tax Information Number (TIN) with their offer. The closing date and time for receipt of quote is 9/14/26 3PM Eastern Standard Time OFFERORS MUST SUBMIT THE FOLLOWING INFORMATION ON THEIR QUOTE: Disclosure: The offeror under this solicitation represents that [Check one]: __ it is not a foreign incorporated entity that should be treated as an inverted domestic corporation pursuant to the criteria of (HSAR) 48 CFR 3009.104-70 through 3009.104-73; __ it is a foreign incorporated entity that should be treated as an inverted domestic corporation pursuant to the criteria of (HSAR) 48 CFR 3009.104-70 through 3009.104-73, but it has submitted a request for waiver pursuant to 3009.104-74, which has not been denied; or __it is a foreign incorporated entity that should be treated as an inverted domestic corporation pursuant to the criteria of (HSAR) 48 CFR 3009.104-70 through 3009.104-73, but it plans to submit a request for waiver pursuant to 3009.104-74. (g) A copy of the approved waiver, if a waiver has already been granted, or the waiver request, if a waiver has been applied for, shall be attached to the bid or proposal. (End of provision) The following FAR Clauses provisions apply to this solicitation. FAR 52.212-1, Instructions to Offerors-Commercial Items (nov 2023); FAR 52.212-3, Offeror Representations and Certifications-Commercial Items (FEB 2023) with Alternate I. Offeror(s) must include a completed copy of FAR 52.212-3 with their quote. The following FAR Clauses apply to this solicitation. Offerors may obtain full text versions of these clauses electronically at www.arnet.gov.; FAR 52.212-4, Contract Terms and Conditions-Commercial Items (dec 2023); FAR 52.212-5, Contract Terms & Conditions Required to Implement Statutes or Executive Orders-Commercial Items (dec 2023). The following clauses listed within FAR 52.212-5 are applicable: FAR 52.219-6 Notice of Total Small Business Set-Aside (Nov 2020)(15 U.S.C. 644), FAR 52.219-28, Post Award Small Business Program representation (oct2022)(15 U.S.C. 632(a)(2); FAR 52.222-3, Convict Labor (Jun 2003)(E.O. 11755); FAR 52.222-19 Child Labor-Cooperation with Authorities and Remedies (Feb 2016) (E.O. 13126); FAR 52.222-21, Prohibition of Segregated Facilities (April 2015); FAR 52.222-26, Equal Opportunity (April 2015)(E.O. 11246); FAR 52.222-36, Equal Opportunity for workers with disabilities (July 2014); FAR 52.223-18 Contractor Policy to Ban Text Messaging while Driving (Aug 2011) (E.O. 13513); FAR 52.225.1 Buy American Act-Supplies (May 2014); FAR 52.225-3, Buy American Act-Free Trade Agreement (dec 2022)(41 U.S.C. 10a-10d); FAR 52.225-13, Restrictions on Certain Foreign Purchases (Jun 2008); 52.232-33, Payment by Electronic Funds Transfer-Central Contractor Registration (July 2013)(31 U.S.C. 3332).
